title: Still Blue On Tuesday
mood: wild, giddy and still covered in paint
subject: turning up to the office on Tuesday still blue from J'ouvert paint after Labor Day in Brooklyn
caption: Power soca in the Brooklyn Labor Day carnival style. A driving four-on-the-floor kick with syncopated snare and tom fills; iron brake-drum percussion ringing on steady eighths; a steelpan playing the main riff over a punchy brass-section line; a bright sawtooth synth lead doubling the brass on the drop; a crowd breakdown where everything stops except the iron. Loud, bright and wide, the kick and iron forward, the brass high in the mix. Male voice, a Trinidadian-English road-march chanter, shouting commands and singing the hook while a crowd answers every line. 156 BPM, G major. Wild, giddy and still covered in paint. No reggaeton dembow, no afrobeats guitar, no dancehall one-drop, no trap hi-hats, no autotune.
lyrics:
[Intro - iron and steelpan riff, kick enters]

[Verse 1]
Monday morning, six o'clock on Flatbush Avenue
J'ouvert, somebody throw a bucket of blue
In my ears, in my teeth, in my good white sneakers
I was jumping on the road till the sun come through

[Pre-Chorus]
Wave! (Wave!)
Jump! (Jump!)

[Chorus]
Still blue on Tuesday (Blue!)
Boss in the meeting looking at my ears (Blue!)
Scrubbed it three times and it won't come off
Still blue on Tuesday

[Verse 2]
Rode the 2 train blue and everybody knew
Lady from Grenada say you play mas, you?
Laptop open on the spreadsheet, I'm a professional
Blue fingerprints on every key

[Pre-Chorus]
Wave! (Wave!)
Wine! (Wine!)

[Chorus]
Still blue on Tuesday (Blue!)
HR send a email, subject paint (Blue!)
Scrubbed it four times and it won't come off
Still blue on Wednesday

[Breakdown - everything stops except the iron]
Everybody who still blue, put your hand up!
(Hand up!)

[Outro - full band, then iron alone]
Still blue, still blue
Next year I'm going green
